weaknesses.point: The manuscript presents an extensive combinatorial enumeration of states and transitions (over 2000 states) without providing any justification or simplification strategy; the sheer size of the state space makes it impossible to verify correctness or to assess the relevance of the included microstates.

The kinetic parameters (binding, unbinding, cleavage, ligation rates) are chosen arbitrarily to satisfy qualitative behavior (e.g., hierarchy of off‑rates) but are not grounded in experimental data or calibrated against any measurable ATPase kinetics; this undermines the claim that the model captures realistic allosteric coupling.

The model assumes that mechanical equilibrium and absence of elastic bias hold for all intermediate states, yet the construction of the linkage network does not demonstrate that the proposed bar additions/removals preserve rigidity or flexibility as claimed; no mechanical analysis (e.g., rigidity percolation) is provided.

The definition of the catalytic cleavage and ligation events as simple bar removals/additions ignores the chemical nature of ATP hydrolysis and product release; the model treats them as instantaneous topological changes without accounting for energy barriers or thermodynamic consistency.

The simulation results focus solely on counting turnover events and identifying futile cycles, but no quantitative comparison to experimental ATPase turnover rates or processivity is offered; the lack of validation limits the biological relevance of the findings.

The manuscript introduces numerous auxiliary constructs (e.g., “idling”, “steric displacement”) that are defined post hoc from simulation data; these concepts are not clearly linked to measurable biochemical phenomena and may reflect overfitting of the model to the simulation outcomes.

The assumption that all reaction rates remain constant throughout the cycle ignores possible allosteric modulation of kinetic parameters that occurs in real ATPases; this simplification may preclude capturing essential dynamic features such as load dependence or cooperative effects.

The discussion of “negative allosteric coupling” relies on geometric constraints of the linkage model, yet the manuscript does not provide a systematic analysis of how robust this coupling is to perturbations in bar lengths or node positions; sensitivity analysis is absent.

The manuscript claims that the design can be extended to synthetic systems, but no concrete mapping to DNA, protein, or polymeric components is provided; the proposed linkage architecture remains purely abstract.
